title: The Sentence Finished

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: A hand held back from the iron is still a hand that knows where the iron stands. The kiln takes four pulls and leaves the fifth where nobody looks; the river counts water over water and enters nothing. A sentence allowed to finish is a sentence nobody can be made to give back.
epigraph.attribution: A saying of the Clay Yard, spoken at the second working of Tallow

where: Low Kiln and the Weir, Sill
pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a one-hundred-and-sixty-to-one-hundred-and-sixty-two-day-old body carried everywhere, told by nobody; the surgeon's register colours the noticing (the firing as a theatre he cannot enter with heat kept and counted behind a screen, the damper's two bites, the carrying arm as a record in muscle that keeps weight and not cost, the date given where a figure was asked as a chart closed over its finding) without a present-tense Chicago break or a tagged remembered line --- the old life stays offstage --- and there is no departure from his eyes, no Court, collector, back-room interior, Marra in Sill, tenth stopping, seventh hearing, calling of the loan, spending of the seventh year or ending; the foundling stays offstage, the green is never Fenna in narration, and no name, figure or payer is given to any withholding

scenes.title: The Working Day After the Reading
scenes.synopsis: First entry, first dated heading and drop capital of the chapter: Day 160, Tallow 11, Firstday, before first grey through mid-morning under the Vail kiln-house roof, at the hearth, the kiln mouth and in the Clay Yard. The boy is one hundred and sixty days old and five months and ten days and nobody under any roof says so (T071/T072). The first Account-day is behind him and is not revisited or recapped; the first smell is hot clay under tallow and the first sound the kiln's breath with its gap, not a bell. Sella feeds the fire under the back of a broken pot and it answers four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for a hundred and sixty days (T058/T079, T088). The widow's mark hangs where it hung, untouched, because a morning and a shelf are not openings; every instruction goes to the wool, the fire, the pot and the broom and never to the basket, and she says the house where another woman would say I, with the half-pace kept from every open slate. The yard goes around the clean dark line, the finer grey called the thaw, the rack space with its broken birth-slates and the empty place in the returning line where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, with a look and a wide step and no number; the trough at the well stands bare and dark and the water is called weather, and the clay jar stands cold under its glaze, glanced at once and not touched (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried). Tarn takes the broom only after it is instructed, six counted where the house can check and the seventh at the lip of the sill where it cannot, no collector on the road, nine stoppings still nine and the loan uncalled (T036/T076, T061/T082). The boy reads the firing as a theatre he cannot enter --- heat kept and counted behind a screen, a gate with two bites, a cost paid by a man whose name is not spoken --- and reaches an inch toward the note of water over water and comes down with one hundred and sixty exact and unspent (T062). Advances T071/T072 (160 exact), T088, T058/T079, T009/T013/T092, T098, T036/T076, T061/T082 and T062.

scenes.title: What the Fire Keeps
scenes.synopsis: Second entry and dated heading of Day 160, Tallow 11, Firstday, afternoon into the going of the light and the small hours under the Vail kiln-house roof at the loaf shelf from the basket's low angle and the hearth. The household's arithmetic stays in loaves pushed along a board, a glance at the clay jar cold under its glaze and a space at the row's end nobody calls a number; a neighbour with a wet pot asks what a firing costs set down there and is sent to the pot with Ask the pot what a wet thing costs set down there. The house has said it, and carries the unanswered question away level so nothing slops (T077). Standing with her back to the basket and moving her lips along the row, Sella reaches a finger BENEATH the front edge where the charcoal tally lies, without looking and without a word, and brings it away without going back to the shelf; the boy sees the hand go under and come back and sees nothing of what the marks say, for such a hand either knows the board by heart or has been told not to look, and the reason stands between the two (T100 carried, unread). The shelf keeps two unnamed gaps, no third comes, and the stiff brown-edged crust lies two inches from his ear with its empty place beside it still unnamed and no third (T060/T086); the pan's gone place keeps the round shape of its absence on a tray of its own, not laid across the shelf's gaps, the fold's crust, the field's empty place, the sixth colour or the sixth shape (T097 held, no fourth likeness made a cause). At the hearth she tells the fire it was the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it, stands a moment counting under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist (the grey streak pale off the coals), sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand and does not look toward the bed; the fire gives four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for a hundred and sixty days (T088, T058/T079). She does not touch the widow's mark because a dusk is not an opening, sets him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without looking at his face and leaves the thread frozen and unwiped, her hand resting a half-beat longer than the setting needs. In the small hours his file is exact and worthless: six hearings beside and never among with no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and not paid, the older intervals, nine stoppings with no payer named to any and no tenth before the seventh year is earned, the damper's double bite joined to no kiln, the two shut-room tellings with no third and the told bell beside the heard bell (T061/T082, T036/T076). One hundred and sixty stands exact and unspent; the charcoal waits under the shelf for a hand that is not his and a day that has not come. Advances T100, T060/T086, T097, T077, T058/T079, T088, T061/T082, T036/T076 and T071/T072 (160 exact).

scenes.title: The Sentence Finished
scenes.synopsis: Third entry and dated heading of Day 161, Tallow 12, Secondday, before first grey into the morning at the Vail wheel-shed, the flagstones, the cold damper and under the Vail roof. **The chapter's one meaningful change:** for the first time under this roof, Jorra's bent finger does not lead Sella's unfinished sentence at the damper. Three or four unnamed men go low-voiced into the finger's-width-open back room before first grey and Sella carries past at the half-pace, gives the house no name for them, turns no head and does not say the room is cold; the two shut-room tellings stand side by side with no third (T065/T095). Jorra comes through with fine grey slate dust ground small as meal into both forearms past the bent little finger and under the nails, not bone-coloured slip, keeps dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray and asks neither which slate was broken nor whether it was a birth-slate; the broken birth-slates stay under the lowest rack, entered by nobody. He speaks to the wheel before anyone (It doesn't care whose hands. It cares if they're steady), tells a pot You'll do, knows its full note before it leaves the wheel and withholds the knowing from a High Kiln kiln-master who says the pot is singing before its time and that such a pot generally sings itself out early; the knowing goes to the near-full tray, not among the hearings (T035/T031, T061/T082). Then, with the fire low and Sella's sentence unfinished, his bent finger goes to the cold iron and STOPS: he stands with his hand on it until she has finished telling him the fire is low, and only then moves the tongue a hair's breadth and leaves it standing. The household straightens around a sentence that was allowed to finish as it has straightened around his silences for three years, but the fraction is real and nobody says a word of it: the boy files it as a change held and not spoken, not a reconciliation and not a hearing, with no payer named to it, and the equality under the roof has moved by that much (T035/T031, T062, T061/T082). Tarn's stroke goes on over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch without the half-check, the stones keeping the place where it stopped, and neither man asks about the ear or the room; the two silences stay unjoined and the loan is uncalled (T036/T076). The boy reads one piece of iron with two bites, the holding and the taking, with no Grathic word for both mercies, filed as an object joined to no kiln beside the two shut-room tellings (T062, T065/T095). The pan's gone place, the shelf's two gaps, the fold's one crust and its empty place and the field's empty place stay on separate trays, no third gap comes, no fourth likeness is made a cause and the charcoal stays unread (T060/T086, T097, T100). Advances T035/T031, T062, T061/T082, T065/T095, T036/T076, T060/T086, T097, T100, T088 and T071/T072 (161 exact).

scenes.title: Nine, Still Nine
scenes.synopsis: Fourth entry and dated heading of Day 161, Tallow 12, Secondday, the going of the light and the small hours under the Vail kiln-house roof at the loaf shelf, the hearth, the kindling and the bed. Sella moves her lips along the loaf row standing with two unnamed gaps, glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze, sends a woman asking what the firing costs to the pot with the house's own answer and gives nobody a figure; she does not go back to the shelf that night, and the charcoal stays where it is, unread and unjoined (T077, T100, T060/T086). At the hearth she tells the fire it was the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it, counts under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist, the grey streak pale off the coals, sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand and does not look toward the bed; the fire gives four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for a hundred and sixty-one days (T058/T079, T088). Tarn takes the broom only after it has been given its instruction and says Yes, house to an early thaw and a late while going on wanting the late because it puts off the paying; at the kindling, with the coals banked and the small knife set back at the very edge of its sill where six are counted and the seventh is held where the house cannot check it, he tells the wood Six counted. The next I don't count. The ear-sentence about an ear under this roof being worth more than the debt that holds it is not brought to the word that would call the loan on this day; the Seed 16 breath stays unspent, no tenth stopping stands up to join the nine, Garl's unforged collector sentence stays beside the knife, and the loan that can hear remains uncalled (T036/T076, T061/T082). In the small hours the file comes back exact, complete and worthless: six hearings beside and never among with no seventh and none invented, three near-full answers advanced and not paid with Jorra's withheld knowing among them, nine stoppings as objects and not a rule with no payer named to any, the damper's double bite joined to no kiln, the two shut-room tellings with no third, the told bell beside the heard bell, the crust and its gap, the two shelf gaps, the pan's gone place, a sixth colour and a sixth shape all on places of their own (T061/T082, T036/T076, T060/T086, T097, T050/T051 held, T033/T034 held). One hundred and sixty-one stands exact and unspent as his hand goes up an inch toward the note of water over water through the finger's-width door and comes down against the fold. Advances T036/T076, T061/T082, T058/T079, T088, T071/T072 (161 exact), T077, T100, T060/T086 and T097; nothing paid.

scenes.title: A Date Where a Figure Was Asked
scenes.synopsis: Fifth entry, dated heading and chapter close: Day 162, Tallow 13, Thirdday, morning into the going of the light downriver at the Weir --- the plank walk on posts, the flat blessing stone, the lower boards, the fish-trade shade below the sill and the out-of-line landing below the north bridge --- and the small hours under the Vail roof. The reed work is finished and has become a direction counted in the arm that carries it, which knows the weight and not the cost; a cost asked as a direction is answered with the river and the weather and leaves no entry (T071/T072, T077). Sella sets the basket at the edge of the work where no slate lies, gives the instruction to the wool and the running water and never to the basket, and keeps the half-pace (T058/T079). The reed-cutter straightens his grey cord on the blessing stone, turns it once, ties one low with his teeth and puts it back inside his coat with the flat of the hand; no knot counted, no figure read (T099 carried). Orra Weir, hands like old rope, pale eel scars uncovered, salt white at her wrists, the nasal half-song of the Fen where she is tired, pulls one knot down with a small flat knock and gives a date where a figure is asked --- the ninth of Ilmen, the collector's boat round the bend on the flood with six oars and one man at the stern who never touched them --- and to the answer that it is not the levy says It's a date. The river takes what the Court doesn't. You can shout at either one. I've tried; the forty-first double turn stays legible, tail tucked, left over right with the weight of a thumb, and the word forty is unspoken, and whether the thumb's return is a lie or the habit of counting the boy does not decide (T024/T059/T025). Mira Silt answers the thin-run question with her own question and answer, flicks eel-bones while deciding whether to lie, keeps her small smile shut like a door on the latch and shows the second twist twice beneath the creel with neither knot counted, her board beside Orra's and not touching (T059/T025). Below the sill a child's foot stays dark inside three turns of wool; the cold to one woman and weather to the yard, with the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody will perform, the surgeon's reading of the extremity going before the core and buying nothing, and no silt-leach, cause or cure named (T093/T094/T096). At the out-of-line landing the soft-cuffed clerk stays set for a measure nobody called, his cuff grey from washing and grey again by midday, his slate turned inward and his hand to it before his eyes to the stalls; nobody has taken him off and nobody makes a fall of the girl who takes the landing sideways (T090/T080). At the going of the light Sella carries him home at the half-pace, goes around the pan's gone place, the bare dark trough and wide around the rack space, sets him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without looking at his face, leaves the thread frozen and unwiped, tells the fire it was the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it, counts under her breath toward no opening, sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand and does not touch the widow's mark because a dusk is not an opening; the two rooms do not touch (T058/T079). In the small hours the file holds six hearings beside and never among with no seventh, nine stoppings with no payer named to any and no tenth before the seventh year is earned, the damper's double bite joined to no kiln, the two shut-room tellings with no third, the told bell beside the heard bell, the crust and its empty place, the two shelf gaps and the pan's gone place on separate trays, and three counts in three places --- the river's note of water over water, the fire's four and a gap, the boards' four nails, four and a knot --- that do not become one (T061/T082, T036/T076, T060/T086, T097). One hundred and sixty-two stands exact, complete and unspent as his hand goes up an inch toward the note of water over water through the finger's-width door and comes down against the fold, the fire misses its fifth under the floor with its payer unnamed for a hundred and sixty-two days, and the charcoal waits under the shelf for a hand that is not his and a day that has not come (T071/T072, T088). Nothing joined, paid, named, opened, called or ended; the chapter pulls forward into Day 163, Tallow 14, and the second working week of the firing month. Advances T071/T072 (162 exact), T077, T058/T079, T099, T024/T059/T025, T093/T094/T096, T090/T080, T061/T082, T036/T076, T088, T060/T086 and T097.
